title: Given a circular array of integers where the end wraps around to the beginning, find the maximum sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray, allowing the subarray to wrap around. Solve it with a combination of maximum and minimum Kadane and demonstrate with a complete banking mini-project.
keyPoints: The best circular sum is max(maxKadane, total - minKadane), covering both non-wrapping and wrapping cases.
A wrapping subarray equals the total minus the non-wrapping middle segment with the smallest sum.
The all-negative edge case requires a guard: if maxKadane < 0, return maxKadane directly.
Without the guard, total - minKadane becomes zero (empty subarray), which violates non-empty requirement.
All three values (maxKadane, minKadane, total) can be computed in a single pass.
Time complexity is O(N) with O(1) space.

s1_definition.oneliner: The best circular sum is the larger of the normal Kadane maximum and the total minus the minimum subarray, with an all-negative guard.
s1_definition.profdef:
- A subarray in a circular array is either **non-wrapping** or **wrapping** (suffix + prefix).
- Non-wrapping: found by standard **max Kadane**.
- Wrapping: equals the **total minus the minimum subarray** (remove the worst middle).
- Answer: `max(maxKadane, total - minKadane)`.
- **All-negative guard**: if `maxKadane < 0`, return `maxKadane` (the least-negative element).
- Compute all three values in **one pass**: O(N) time, O(1) space.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Rajesh reviews a repeating weekly cycle of daily net cash flows that wraps from Sunday back to Monday. He wants the most profitable continuous stretch, which might start late in one week and continue into the next. A wrapping stretch is the whole week minus some unwanted middle slump. He finds the best non-wrapping stretch the normal way, and separately finds the worst middle slump to carve out, and takes whichever gives more.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The maximum sum circular subarray problem asks for the largest sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray in a circular array where the subarray may wrap from the end back to the start. The insight is that any subarray has one of two shapes: non-wrapping (handled by max Kadane) or wrapping (handled by removing the worst middle segment from the total, which is total minus min Kadane).

You compute three values in one pass: the maximum subarray sum, the minimum subarray sum, and the total. The answer is the larger of the max Kadane result and the total minus the min Kadane result. The one critical edge case is the all-negative array: when every element is negative, total minus min Kadane becomes zero (empty subarray), so you return the max Kadane result directly.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this on the treasury desk where settlement cycles were circular. Daily net cash flows wrapped from the last day of the cycle back to the first, and the team needed the most profitable continuous stretch even if it crossed the cycle boundary. The two-Kadane decomposition found both the non-wrapping and wrapping best stretches in one pass.

The senior-level insight is the removal reframing: wrapping equals total minus the worst middle. This reframing is what many candidates miss, and the all-negative guard is the single detail that separates a correct solution from one that silently returns zero.

Remember one sentence: the best circular subarray sum is max(maxKadane, total - minKadane), with a guard returning maxKadane when all elements are negative.
